title: Semi-supervised learning selects a lithium thioborate for vacancy engineering
summary: Semi-supervised learning screened lithium-containing structures and selected Li3BS3 for experimental characterization. The parent material was a poor room-temperature conductor. Researchers then introduced vacancies by Si substitution and amorphized the substituted material; the paper reports approximately four orders of magnitude higher ionic conductivity for a-Li2.95B0.95Si0.05S3. The model selected the framework, while human-led defect engineering produced the high-conductivity sample. This does not establish that pristine Li3BS3 is superionic.

evidence.tested: The study selected Li3BS3 for characterization and reports increased ionic conductivity after Si substitution and amorphization, with the combined vacancy-engineering treatment improving conductivity by roughly four orders of magnitude.
evidence.unknown: The ML model selected a framework candidate; vacancy engineering and synthesis were subsequent researcher-led steps. The primary page was checked through indexed full-text results because direct article opening returned 403.
evidence.ai_role: Semi-supervised learning used literature-derived conductivity labels and structural descriptors to rank lithium-containing structures and select Li3BS3 for experimental characterization.
